Investigation is complete and a fix is up in PR #17979.

What changed:
- added a coalescing SSE relay for `/event`, `/global/event`, and the workspace control-plane event stream

- added relay regression tests

presumably larger and better LLMs will be less likely to get caught in loops. I've had great luck with qwen3-coder-next which seems to me to be the best agentic OW model right now, however, once in a while it still appears to get caught in loops. I'm sure there are other strategies beyond explicit loop detection which would still help with loops (ideas?), and obviously properly configured models will be less loopy - but yeah explicit loop detection just seems like the most straight forward solution to a real problem I've experienced.

Oh yeah also with wrt other agentic systems (minimax/codex/claudecode) those systems are typically specifically tuned to be working with a very narrow set of models, and I also wouldnt be surprised if the minimax agent also has this issue and simply hasn't addressed it. I see opencode as more generalised system, and as such I think it makes sense to allow for optional mechanisms which address some of the looping problems folks have experienced. Optional is key btw, if somebody is using a great frontier model and paying dearly for it, they probably don't need or want loop detection, I'm just not one of those people.

### Update: Root Cause Found

I have identified the cause of the hang during startup. The issue is specifically related to the environment where the `%TEMP%` / `%TMP%` environment variables are pointed to a **RAM Disk** (created via OSFMount).

#### Findings:
- **The Trigger:** When `%TEMP%` is set to a RAM Disk, `opencode` (and its internal `npm` processes) hangs indefinitely during the initialization phase.
- **The Workaround:** Temporarily redirecting `%TEMP%` to a local NTFS drive (e.g., `C:\local_temp`) allows the application to start normally.
- **Observations on Security:** Although some users suggested security software interference, I am using **ESET** and observed **no notifications or logs** regarding blocked files. This suggests the hang is likely not a proactive block, but rather an I/O deadlock.

#### Technical Hypothesis:
This behavior might be due to how Node.js or the underlying terminal bridge handles file locking, symbolic links, or change notifications (`ReadDirectoryChangesW`) on non-standard file systems. If the RAM Disk's NTFS emulation doesn't perfectly match the expectations of the Node.js event loop, it can lead to the "silent hang" observed in the title bar (e.g., stuck on `npm config get registry`).

#### Conclusion:
Since I have found a workaround for my environment, I am happy to close this issue if you consider this a "won't fix" due to the niche nature of RAM Disk configurations. 

However, if the team is interested in investigating the robustness of I/O handling on virtual/RAM drives, I will leave this open for your further assessment. Please let me know if I should close this or provide any specific logs while the RAM Disk is active.

> These lags occur when you have `systemd-timesyncd` enabled.
> 
> What happens is that WSL will adjust the time differently than Windows, and Hyper-V correcting time back into the past - which causes corrupt timestamps, freezes in the client, as Javascript timeouts will suddenly wait seconds.
> 
> Try `sudo systemctl disable systemd-timesyncd && sudo systemctl stop systemd-timesyncd`

I want to provide a insight into my journey towards having the opencode.json saved finally at the correct location:

When trying to find out, how to add a specific LMStudio adress, I got caught up in looking for the opencode.json inside ~/.config/opencode/

That looked like a normal node project directory to me, so I thought that should definitely not be it and there was no default opencode.json or opencode.example.json so I looked elsewhere.

I somehow found out that there is ~/.local/share/opencode/ and ~/.local/state/opencode/

In each I put the opencode.json and that did not work. Then after further research I stumbled on this thread and finally found out: I have to create the opencode.json inside the directory myself. That directory that I assumed was wrong from the start: ~/.config/opencode/

I hope this might provide further information on how the process on the discovery of opencode.json might unfold.

I implemented this on my branch and am opening a PR for it.

My main motivation was using the [context-mode](https://github.com/mksglu/context-mode) plugin with OpenCode so it can restore one-shot session context automatically instead of requiring manual setup each time.

The implementation adds `session.start` with `startup`, `resume`, and `compact` triggers, stores pending hook context on the session, and injects it into the next LLM turn. I also added tests for the core hook behavior, resume wiring, and the fork startup timing edge case.

One tradeoff in the current implementation: pending context is consumed lazily on the next model turn, so resume-triggered context can become stale if a session is resumed but not prompted soon after. I documented that in code/comments rather than broadening the scope of this PR.

# OpenCode Permissions Testing

Test repository for validating OpenCode's file system permissions and git operations.

## Purpose

This repository helps verify that OpenCode can:

- Create directories and files
- Initialize git repositories
- Commit changes
- Push to remote repositories
- Handle branch operations

## Testing Workflow

Test basic git operations:

```bash
# Verify repository status
git status

# Create a test commit
echo "test" > test.txt
git add test.txt
git commit -m "test: add test file"

# Check commit history
git log --oneline
```

Test remote operations:

```bash
# Add remote (replace with your repository URL)
git remote add origin <url>

# Push to remote
git push -u origin main
```

## Common Permission Issues

**Directory creation fails** - Check that OpenCode has write access to the target directory.

**Git operations fail** - Verify git is configured with user name and email.

**Push fails** - Ensure SSH keys or credentials are properly configured.
